summary.intent: Execute Phase 35 of the cipher-box project: migrate the TEE worker to Phala Cloud CVM infrastructure, including monorepo restructuring, testing, observability, CI/CD updates, and initial CVM deployment and verification.
summary.outcome: Phase 35 fully completed across 6 plans and 4 waves. TEE worker moved to apps/tee-worker/ with shared packages, 56 unit tests added, Phala SDK integrated, staging CI/CD updated, CVM deployed and verified on Phala Cloud production infra. Security review conducted with all HIGH/MEDIUM findings fixed. PR #395 created with lint, review comments, and code quality issues resolved.

repo: The project uses a GSD (get-shit-done) workflow system with wave-based parallel plan execution via subagents, coordinated through .planning/ directory artifacts
TEE worker was restructured from root tee-worker/ into apps/tee-worker/ as part of this phase, following monorepo conventions
Phala Cloud has no separate testnet — the free tier ($20 credit) runs on the same production infrastructure (Intel TDX hardware, prod5 nodes) as paid deployments; phase was misnamed 'testnet'
Docker is not available on the dev machine (runs on separate host 192.168.133.12); image builds require SSH to that host or CI pipeline
The entire/ branch stores conversation transcripts checkpointed automatically — secrets shared in conversation will be captured in these transcripts
SSRF validation uses ssrfSafeFetch with DNS pinning via undici Agent custom lookup to prevent DNS rebinding attacks against cloud metadata endpoints
Auth middleware uses timingSafeEqual with length pre-check for constant-time token comparison
multiformats package (CID.parse) is available in @cipherbox/crypto and should be used for CID validation instead of hand-rolled regex
sdk-core pinning index.ts was missing FetchFn re-export, requiring consumers to use ProviderOptions['fetchFn'] or deep-import

code.finding: Was calling getKeypair() instead of getPublicKey(), leaking private key into route scope — critical security bug fixed during /simplify review
Was reading TEE_EPOCH env var but migrate route uses TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH — inconsistent naming bug fixed
Added MAX_BATCH_SIZE=100 guard to prevent unbounded ECIES decryption DoS; removed dead keyEpoch field; derived successes/failures from results array instead of mutable counters
404 fallback label must be '/:unmatched' (not 'unmatched') to match the API's http-metrics.interceptor.ts:40 pattern and prevent unbounded Prometheus label cardinality

DNS pinning was implemented by rewriting the URL hostname to resolved IP, which breaks TLS SNI/certificate validation. Fixed by using undici Agent with custom lookup function that pins DNS without changing the request URL
SSRF protocol check compared 'endpoint' variable instead of 'protocol' against 'cipherbox' — would never match, defeating the SSRF bypass for internal cipherbox:// protocol
Epoch key cache had no bounds — added MAX_CACHE_SIZE=100 and epoch range validation (1-10000) to prevent memory growth and invalid inputs

Migrate route was reading TEE_CURRENT_EPOCH once at module load (stale after rotation) — fixed to read from request body with env var fallback; also replaced hand-rolled CID regex with CID.parse() from multiformats
Public index re-exported PinningProvider, PinResult, PinStatus, PinningMode, ExternalProviderConfig, ConnectionTestResult, ProviderOptions but omitted FetchFn — added FetchFn to the export list

workflow: GSD pause-work/resume-work workflow successfully transferred context between sessions across machines via HANDOFF.json — effective for cross-device session handoff
Secrets shared in conversation (API keys, tokens) are captured in entire/ branch transcript checkpoints — rotate immediately after session if they appear in conversation messages
Wave-based parallel subagent execution causes git config lock conflicts — sequential execution for plans within a wave is safer in practice
The classifyHandoffIfNeeded Claude Code bug can cause agents to report failure even after successful completion — spot-check via SUMMARY.md existence and git log to verify
Worktree merge conflicts in STATE.md and ROADMAP.md are common when multiple subagents run in parallel — take the most recent agent's version for these files
/simplify review caught a critical private key exposure bug (getKeypair vs getPublicKey) — security-critical routes should always be reviewed
Security review should be run before creating PR, not after — finding bugs post-PR requires additional fix commits
pnpm workspace hoisting can cause TypeScript to fail resolving explicitly added packages — verify tsconfig paths or use static imports

friction: Usage limits hit mid-Wave 2 execution, interrupting parallel agent runs for plans 35-02 and 35-03 — required manual retry sequentially
git config lock errors prevented parallel worktree agent execution — had to fall back to sequential spawning
gsd-tools init runs relative to CWD and fails when not in the project root — required explicit path resolution from worktree
HANDOFF.json captured credentials (Phala API key, TEE worker secret) in plaintext — both needed immediate rotation after discovery
undici types not auto-resolved in pnpm workspace despite explicit dependency add — required static import to resolve TypeScript errors
entire/ branch transcript checkpoint automatically captured credentials shared in conversation — no mechanism to scrub before push
Merge conflicts in ROADMAP.md and STATE.md from main required manual resolution after PR was already created
Docker not available on dev machine required either SSH to Docker host or CI pipeline for image builds — added coordination complexity to the checkpoint plan
open_items: SSRF probe deduplication: connection-test.ts has similar probe logic to sdk-core — significant refactor deferred
The existing CVM on Phala Cloud prod5 is running with the old (now-rotated) credentials until next staging-v* tag push triggers redeploy
HUMAN-UAT.md for Phase 35 has status: partial — will surface in /gsd:progress and /gsd:audit-uat until explicitly verified
Phase directory named 35-phala-testnet-tee-migration is a permanent misnomer — renaming would break all cross-references, accepted as-is with documentation correction
Security review LOW-02 (health endpoint discloses mode/epoch info) accepted as operational necessity — not addressed
String zeroing for auth tokens is fundamentally ineffective in JS (strings are immutable) — acknowledged limitation, no workaround possible without refactoring to Uint8Array throughout
